insights.headline: Gold slips below $3,600 as silver tests $40 on tariff fears
insights.summary: Spot gold fell to about $3,565 an ounce and silver to $40.77, a fresh 14-month low, as reported US tariff-hike plans and a fresh AI-stock slide spurred liquidity selling. On MCX, December gold ended the evening session down 2.8% at Rs 1,22,505 and silver down 5.7% at Rs 1,45,406. Traders now watch Wednesday's US core PCE at 19:00 IST, the next test before the Fed's 9 December decision.
points: Spot gold fell below $3,600 toward $3,550 as reported US tariff-hike plans and an AI-stock slide spurred liquidity selling, FXEmpire reports.
Silver tested $40.50–$41.00 support as the gold/silver ratio neared 87; spot silver stood at $40.77, a fresh 14-month low.
MCX December gold ended the evening session down 2.8% at Rs 1,22,505; silver ended down 5.7% at Rs 1,45,406.
December Fed hike odds near 97% for a quarter point; US core PCE due Wednesday at 19:00 IST.
Silver mine output stays flat in 2026 despite a sixth straight annual deficit of 35 million oz, the Silver Institute and Metals Focus estimate.

trending.title: US session slide extends the rout
trending.summary: Gold slipped below $3,600 and silver tested $40.50–$41.00 in US trading as reported tariff-hike plans and a fresh AI-stock slide spurred liquidity selling, giving back more of Monday's rebound.

trending.title: MCX evening session ends sharply lower
trending.summary: December gold ended the evening session down 2.8% at Rs 1,22,505 and silver down 5.7% at Rs 1,45,406, with the slide linked to growing Fed hike bets and a firm dollar.

trending.title: Silver falls harder than gold, again
trending.summary: Silver is down 39% in 13 weeks, its steepest fall since the Lehman crash, and its 6% MCX slide outpaced gold's 2.9% drop in the evening session, with the gold/silver ratio nearing 87.

trending.title: Silver's supply gap won't close soon
trending.summary: Mine output stays flat in 2026 despite a sixth straight annual deficit, as most silver comes as a byproduct of other metals' mines; weaker solar demand could even tip the market into surplus in 2027.

items.title: Gold (XAUUSD), Silver, Platinum Forecasts – Gold Retreats Below $3600
items.summary: Gold slipped below $3,600 as traders reacted to US plans to raise tariffs on goods from more than a dozen countries and a fresh slide in AI shares. FXEmpire notes gold failed to hold $3,630–$3,650 and drifted toward $3,550. Silver tested $40.50–$41.00 as the gold/silver ratio neared 87, while platinum fell toward $1,250; lower yields and a softer dollar failed to lift gold amid liquidity selling.

items.title: Gold & Silver Rates: MCX gold slumps by Rs 3,671, silver crashes 6% amid growing Fed hike bets
items.summary: MCX December gold fell as much as Rs 3,671, or 2.9%, to Rs 1,22,325 in the evening session and was down 2.8% at Rs 1,22,505 late in the day; December silver slid as much as Rs 9,253, or 6%, to Rs 1,44,964. Zee Business links the slide to growing bets on further Fed rate hikes and a firm dollar.

items.title: Gold Sinks with AI, Silver Extends Worst Drop Since Lehmans as 'Fed Mistake' Looms
items.summary: Gold fell back to $3,560 an ounce, giving back $125 of Monday's $150 rebound, while silver dropped to $40.76, a new 14-month low and its steepest 13-week fall since the Lehman crash of 2008. BullionVault cites rising Fed hike expectations, with traders putting a 97% chance on a December rise, and quotes Bill Ackman calling a December hike a 'mistake'.

items.title: Gold struggles to extend rebound as Fed rate hike bets pressure silver
items.summary: Spot gold was modestly lower and silver sharply lower in early US trading on Tuesday, as a firm dollar and expectations of more Federal Reserve rate hikes pressured metals ahead of key inflation data, Kitco reports. At about 8:37 a.m. EST, gold traded near $3,621.70, down 0.34%, while silver traded near $42.04, down 2.33%; support sits at $3,595 for gold and $41.89 for silver.

items.title: Bullion tumbles again: Gold slips 0.7%, silver nearly 3% down; Three US triggers to watch
items.summary: MCX December gold futures opened 0.7% lower at Rs 1,25,112 per 10 g in the evening session and silver fell 2.35% to Rs 1,50,591 per kg, giving back part of Monday's sharp rebound. Spot gold held just above $3,630 an ounce while silver slipped to about $43, with traders awaiting US PCE inflation ahead of the Fed's December meeting.

items.title: Silver price crash: Rates today in India down ₹1 lakh in 3 months! Recovery or more fall ahead for MCX silver futures?
items.summary: Silver in India is down about ₹1 lakh per kg in three months from its August high of around ₹2.5 lakh, with MCX silver closing Monday at ₹1,54,205 per kg after a ₹6,392 rebound. Market experts attribute the slide to elevated US bond yields, a strong dollar, talk of a US Fed rate hike and the rupee's rise from around 98 to 92.50 per dollar; they put crucial support at ₹1,40,000 per kg.

items.title: Gold edges up on bargain buying after selloff; US inflation data awaited
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.4% to $3,645.29 an ounce in early Asian trade, extending Monday's rebound from a 14-month low, while silver climbed 1.2% to $43.55. Markets now await Wednesday's US PCE inflation data, with traders pricing a 95% chance of a December Fed rate rise.

items.title: Silver miners struggle to close persistent supply gap
items.summary: Silver mine output is set to stay flat in 2026 despite a sixth straight annual deficit, with demand forecast to exceed supply by 35 million oz, Metals Focus estimates. Primary mines supply just 26.1% of output, the rest a byproduct of other metals mines, so higher prices alone are not lifting production. Weaker solar demand could tip the market into surplus in 2027, Deutsche Bank notes.

items.title: Gold slips with spotlight on US inflation data
items.summary: Spot gold slipped 0.5% to $3,611.99 an ounce by 0827 GMT on Tuesday after rising nearly 3% in the previous session, as expectations of further US rate hikes and a dollar near a 20-month high weighed on prices. Silver fell 2.4% to $42.04. Traders now await Wednesday's US PCE inflation data, the last key reading before the Fed's final meeting of 2026.

items.title: Explained: Why Gold prices gained and extended a rebound from a 14-month low - 3 reasons
items.summary: Gold held near $3,630 an ounce on Tuesday after surging 2.7% on Monday, extending a rebound from a 14-month low after last week's near-9% drop. Mint traces the bounce to bargain buying, a rally in global equities after Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's return, and an easing 10-year Treasury yield, with traders awaiting US PCE inflation on Wednesday and watching the Fed's December decision.

items.title: Gold Climbs To Rs 1.28 Lakh Per 10 Grams, Silver Recovers
items.summary: Retail gold climbed to nearly Rs 1.28 lakh per 10 g on Tuesday — 24-carat gold around Rs 1,27,800, up Rs 1,240 — snapping a 10-session losing streak in the national capital, while retail silver hovered near Rs 1.55 lakh per kg. MCX December gold futures settled 3.8% higher at Rs 1,28,912 per 10 g on Monday, and spot gold stood near $3,645 an ounce.

MCX gold futures rose 2.2% and silver 2.11% on Monday after last week's slide — gold fell 11% and silver 16.2% on the week — as short covering and bargain buying met a softer dollar and fading bets on Fed hikes. Spot gold traded near $3,609, up 2%, and silver just above $42. Analysts quoted remain cautious, saying the rebound must hold above resistance to confirm a turn.
items.title: Gold and silver rebound over 2% after steep weekly losses: Can the recovery sustain?

items.summary: MCX December gold futures rose Rs 2,899, or 2.38%, to Rs 1,24,677 per 10 grams as speculators built fresh positions on firm spot demand, PTI reported; silver futures gained 2.45% to Rs 1,51,435 per kg. In New York, gold futures rose 2.14% to $3,614.25 an ounce and silver futures 2.91%.
items.title: Gold futures rise to Rs 1.24 lakh per 10 grams, silver crosses Rs 1.51 lakh per kg
Silver and Copper Retest Lows as Oil Nears Its Turn
items.summary: Silver and copper retested recent lows as the broad metals sell-off extended into the US session, while oil approached a turning point, Investing.com's analysis notes. The piece comes as spot silver tests the $40.50–$41.00 support zone and copper extends its slide alongside precious metals.

items.title: Silver Recovery Watch: Identifying the Next Major Market Turning Point
items.summary: Silver futures steadied near $42.56 after correcting from a recent high near $47.92 to a low of $40.62, the analysis says, with $42.90 the immediate level to reclaim and $43.57 the weekly benchmark for buyers to regain control; holding above $41.68 keeps the recovery intact, while a break below the $40.62 low would point to more weakness.

items.title: World Gold Council brings digital gold trading to life
items.summary: The World Gold Council completed the first live pilot of a digital settlement system for physical gold, with HSBC, JPMorgan and StoneX trading and settling fractional ownership of bullion as collateral through Pooled Gold Interests. The council calls it a historic step for using gold in modern financial markets.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2021-22 Series I premature redemption price at ₹12,612
items.summary: The RBI has fixed the premature redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2021-22 Series I at ₹12,612 per unit for the November 25 redemption, based on the average IBJA 999-purity gold close over November 19, 20 and 23. Holders who applied in the window that closed November 16 can exit at that price, a gain of up to 167% over the ₹4,727 online issue price.

items.title: Indian rupee could rise to 91.50/$ on equity inflows, HDFC Bank's treasury head says
items.summary: The rupee could strengthen to 91.50 per dollar if strong equity inflows continue, HDFC Bank treasury head Arup Rakshit said, seeing it in a 91.50-93.50 range near term. The currency closed Friday at 92.67, up nearly 2.5% in November on record $12 billion of foreign equity inflows, and Rakshit expects the RBI to raise rates in December, with a 25-basis-point hike more or less given.

items.title: Domestic stock markets closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti; MCX to resume trading in evening session
items.summary: MCX will stay shut for its morning session on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti, with gold and silver futures trading resuming in the evening session from 5 pm; NSE and BSE are closed for the day and reopen on Wednesday.

items.title: Salem Anklet manufacturers see a silver lining as metal price dips Rs 2L/ kg in 10 months
items.summary: Salem's silver anklet makers say orders have recovered to nearly half of normal levels after more than a year of sluggish business, as silver fell to about Rs 175 a gram in the city from Rs 195 a week ago, the article reports. Workshops that ran about two days a week now work nearly six days a week ahead of Pongal.
